newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline surges on downed cracker, up $8.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline surges on downed cracker, up $8.

text.p: NWE gasoline grabbed the limelight again on Friday as prices soared by up to $8 a tonne.

The already tight supply situation in NWE was exacerbated by news today that a catalytic cracker at Shell's Pernis refinery in Rotterdam will be down for an unscheduled stoppage in August. A planned two month shut-down has been brought forward to follow the unscheduled stoppage which means the unit will be out for a total of three months.
Around 100,000 tonnes of gasoline production will be lost every month at a time when tight supplies in the U.S. and Europe have been kicking prices higher.
Shell has two catalytic crackers at its Pernis site and some remains working.
"The only way is up after this (the Shell news)," said one trader who said interest for material was strong.
Antwerp barges have traded at $212 and $212.50 while Rotterdam storage has gone at $213.50.
"We are seeing people bidding around $214, thats $8 up on yesterday," said one dealer.

Gasoline swaps were also stronger, gaining $5 or so. Traders said August was pegged around $210. Swaps have not jumped to the same degree as the wet market because more supplies are expected from mid August onwards.
However, with 100,000 tonnes a month missing from Pernis some dealers see no end in sight for gasoline's bull run.
